tasks.title: #284: a corrupt full-length plan table drops only that table
tasks.test_approach: RED first: in tests/test_preprocess.py, beside test_a_geometric_run_leaves_out_an_unreadable_or_non_schema_plan_parquet, (a) write a full-length plan.parquet with its footer thrift bytes overwritten (same file length, trailing <len>PAR1 intact), assert in-test that pq.read_table raises OSError and not ArrowInvalid, then a geometric preprocess run gives ('plan_1','preprocessed',''), no plan.parquet, exactly one REASON_PLAN_INDEX warning, no REASON_IO_ERROR. Must fail on current code. (b) monkeypatch pathlib.Path.read_bytes to raise OSError only for plan.parquet: the patient gets REASON_IO_ERROR. See spec docs/specs/2026-11-12-hardening-sprint.md #284. Test (b) is red on current code (which never calls read_bytes) and needs a geometric run. Corruption recipe: overwrite ~16 bytes just before the trailing <4-byte footer length>PAR1 with 0xFF; if the in-test assert reports ArrowInvalid instead of OSError, corrupt bytes mid-file (a data page) instead, or the snappy block. The stress test confirmed footer, data-page and snappy corruption each raise OSError.

Test (b) passes: a read_bytes OSError gives REASON_IO_ERROR for the patient
The later write's OSError still propagates (not inside the try)
index_plan_table docstring updated to say a parse error of any kind returns False and only a read OSError propagates
Full suite and ruff pass

tasks.title: #295 + #325: fluence and aperture test gaps
tasks.test_approach: Tests only, behavior already correct; each names its red mutation (apply, see red, revert, record in docs/plans/hardening-sprint/findings.md). See spec docs/specs/2026-11-12-hardening-sprint.md #295/#325. (1) call beam_volume.aperture(row) directly with one leaf boundary -> not modelled (mutation: remove only the `len(boundaries) < 2 or` clause; np.all of an empty diff is True). (2) fluence_mu: a not-modelled aperture on a weight-0 control point is refused. Hand-build it: take plan_rows output and set number_of_blocks=1 or mlc_type='MLCY' on the weight-0 row (mutation: call aperture only when weight != 0). (3) float64 accumulation: plan_rows gives control point 0 mu=0, so build the plan through the maps helper with cumulative weights [0, 2^25, 2^25, 2^25+2, 2^25+2, 2^25+4] and BeamMeterset equal to the final weight (MU 0, 2^25, 0, 2, 0, 2; trapezoid weights 2^24, 2^24, 1, 1, 1, 1). Alternatively, hand-build rows with mu=[2^25, 0, 2, 0, 2]. Use integer jaw edges so the checked pixel's overlap is exactly 1.0. The expected pixel is exactly 2^25+4; a float32 accumulator gives 2^25, because float32 spacing there is 4 (mutation: np.float64 -> np.float32 accumulator). (4) exactly-200 mm field accepted at -X, +Y, -Y (mutation: < -LIMIT -> <= -LIMIT, etc.). (5) a SETUP beam sharing a BeamNumber with a treatment beam is accepted (mutation: drop the SETUP filter in the duplicate check). (6) AC1 all-zero-outside checks: the field covers rows 170..229 and columns 150..249, so check a[0,:170], a[0,230:], a[0,:,:150] and a[0,:,250:] are all zero. (7) the convert fluence test at tests/test_convert.py:~2133: pass frame_uid=sd.generate_uid() and assert the compared UID is non-empty. (8) #325: plan_rows refuses duplicate BeamNumbers first, so build rows from a plan without duplicates, then call fluence_mu(dup_plan, rows) where dup_plan has two treatment beams sharing a BeamNumber -> REASON_FLUENCE (mutation: delete the duplicate check). For (3), first check that plan_rows accepts BeamMeterset 2^25+4; if it bounds it, hand-build the rows.
